# SCI-POINT ODQ-009 Scientific-Owner Approval

Record identity: `SCI-POINT-ODQ-009-APPROVAL-2026-09-02`

Scientific owner: Grant Wilson

Decision date: `2026-09-02`

Status: approved Stage A scientific direction; bounded owner-decision set closed

## Approved Named-Use Policy Roles

SCI-POINT and its consumers shall not use one universal good/bad fit flag.
These scientifically distinct policy roles are required:

1. SCI-POINT owns the policy for completeness of its per-array fit result.
2. The named pointing-support producer owns the policy for admitting a POINT
   displacement into correction construction.
3. The named telescope/observing-quality-control process owns its fitted-
   parameter admission, reference, threshold, comparison, aggregation, and
   action policy.
4. CAL or TolProj owns the policy for admitting a POINT amplitude into an
   authorized photometric-transfer use.

The same immutable POINT result may pass one named use, fail another, and
remain diagnostic-only for a third. Diagnostic-only is an explicit use-
specific outcome with the affected claim and reason; it is not a universal
bad-result bit. No POINT-owned whole-observation or cross-array aggregate
profile enters base v0.1.

VAL registers and evaluates the exact named-use policies and source bindings.
VAL does not author, broaden, compose, or silently repair them. Each named-use
owner remains responsible for its policy and actions.

## Stage B Author Assignment

The implementation-blind Stage B author may define collision-free exact
profile identifiers, facts, action names, and pass/fail/unavailable mechanics
consistent with the owner-approved roles and ODQ-001 through ODQ-008. The
scientific owner retains final approval of that exact profile set. Author
freedom does not permit moving policy ownership to VAL or POINT, collapsing
the named uses, inventing an aggregate profile, or changing per-array
atomicity.

## Non-Effects

This approval closes the bounded ODQ-001 through ODQ-009 owner-decision
walkthrough. It does not approve the complete Stage A packet or exact author
input bytes, authorize Stage B, modify a Registry, change an algorithm, or
establish implementation conformity, validation, achieved performance,
readiness, or production state.
